name: Malawi
snapshot: Peter Mutharika returned to power in 2025 promising to fix the economy, but in 2026 fuel prices jumped 40 percent and drivers were again sleeping at empty pumps.
culture: Malawi calls itself "the warm heart of Africa". Lake Malawi, which runs along much of the country, holds more fish species than any other lake. The Gule Wamkulu masked dances of the Chewa people are UNESCO-listed. Chichewa is the national language alongside English.
society: Most Malawians farm small plots, and tobacco is the main export. Chronic shortages of fuel and foreign exchange, and cyclones like Freddy in 2023, have hit the economy. A 2020 court ruling that annulled a flawed election and ordered a rerun was hailed as a landmark for judicial independence in Africa.
situation: In September 2025 voters returned former president Peter Mutharika, 85, who had lost the 2020 rerun to Lazarus Chakwera, amid anger over inflation and shortages. Relief has been slow. His government raised fuel prices by more than 40 percent in January 2026 and aims to bring inflation below 21 percent, but shortages of fuel and foreign currency persisted, and by October motorists were queuing overnight at dry filling stations. Chakwera's MCP accuses the government of ignoring the hardship.
power: A presidential republic. The president is directly elected for five years and, since a 2020 court ruling, needs more than half the vote; parliament is unicameral.
